successors.name: House of Habsburg
successors.text: Cliopatria's Habsburg shape from 1279 (79,610 km2) covers Austria and Styria; the 1260-1278 Habsburg shapes are Swiss

ledger.x: c. 960: Otto I sets up the Eastern March below the Enns. 'by about 960, he appointed Burchard as margrave' of a new Eastern March, after the Lechfeld (955); some sources give 970 and the infobox dates the margraviate from c. 970. The Danube lands had been lost beyond the Enns in 907. Repair of 2026-10-25: the founding…

c. 960: the Eastern March is a Bavarian march. 'by about 960, he appointed Burchard as margrave'; the page calls it the Bavarian Eastern March and has it 'elevated to a duchy independent from Bavaria by the Privilegium Minus' in 1156. Recorded from the vassal's side: the counterpart is the overlord, the mirror of…
976: Otto II deposes Burchard and appoints Leopold the Illustrious of the Babenberg house as margrave; the Babenbergs rule Austria until 1246.
Between 1018 and 1055 (bridged at 1043): the march reaches the March (Morava) and the Leitha.
1055: the northern Waldviertel and the northern Weinviertel come into the march.
1108 (bridged): the residence moves from Melk to Klosterneuburg.
1145: Vienna becomes the capital; the residence had stayed at Klosterneuburg 'until 1145, when Vienna became the official capital'.
17 September 1156: 'Austria was elevated to a duchy independent from Bavaria by the Privilegium Minus' (Margraviate of Austria page); the mirror of stem-duchy-of-bavaria's vassal_end.
1246: the personal union with Styria ends with the Babenbergs.
1251: Ottokar II of Bohemia takes Austria.
1276: Rudolf of Habsburg takes the dominion.
1282: Rudolf I grants the Austrian domains to his sons Albert and Rudolf II at the Diet of Augsburg; Albert I's reign is listed as 1282-1291.

wars.name: Battle of the Leitha River
wars.outcome: Duke Frederick II was killed in 1246 and the Babenberg line became extinct in the male line; the succession was fought over until Ottokar II of Bohemia took the duchy in 1250-1251.

wars.name: Battle on the Marchfeld
wars.outcome: Rudolf I took over the dominion in 1276; Ottokar II was killed by the united Austrian and Hungarian forces at the Marchfeld on 26 August 1278.

certainty.note: No treaty draws the march's frontiers on the pages opened; the Privilegium Minus names no counties and the page gives no borders for Austria.
